h: Toldos Ois 1 · The Patriarchs Crown One Another

p: "וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק וְגוֹמֵר",
“And these are the generations of Isaac, etc.”
בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא:
In Midrash Tanchuma:
זֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב:
This is what Scripture stated:
"גִּיל יָגִיל אֲבִי צַדִּיק וְגוֹמֵר",
“The father of a righteous person shall greatly rejoice, etc.,”
כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק,
corresponding to Isaac,
שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק הָיוּ הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים:
for at the time Isaac was born, all were rejoicing:
שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ, חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה, כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כוּלֵי,
heaven and earth, sun and moon, stars and constellations, etc.,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
as it is said:
"אִם לֹא בְרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ לֹא שָׂמְתִּי",
“If not for My covenant day and night, the statutes of heaven and earth I would not have appointed,”
וְאֵין בְּרִיתִי אֶלָּא יִצְחָק כוּלֵי.
and “My covenant” refers solely to Isaac, etc.
נִרְאֶה דְּהַמִּדְרָשׁ מְפָרֵשׁ "יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה" – חַמָּה וּלְבָנָה;
It appears that the Midrash interprets “day and night” as the sun and the moon;
"חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ" – הַיְינוּ כּוֹכָבִים חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁקְּבוּעִים בַּשָּׁמַיִם,
“the statutes of heaven and earth”—meaning the stars are the statutes of heaven which are fixed in the heavens,
וּמַזָּלוֹת חֻקּוֹת אָרֶץ, שֶׁעִיקַּר שִׁימּוּשׁ הַמַּזָּלוֹת בְּהַנְהָגַת הָאָרֶץ.
and the constellations are the statutes of the earth, as the primary function of the constellations is in governing the earthly realm.
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְהָבִין שַׁיָּיכוּת פְּתִיחָה זוֹ לְפָרָשַׁת "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק",
Yet one must understand the connection of this introductory exposition to the portion of “These are the generations of Isaac,”
כֵּיוָן דִּלְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ נִרְאֶה דְּדָרַשׁ "אֲבִי צַדִּיק" עַל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה אָבִיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק,
since according to its simple reading it would appear that it expounds “the father of a righteous person” as referring to our father Abraham, peace be upon him, who was the father of Isaac,
וְהָיָה יוֹתֵר שַׁיָּיךְ דְּרָשָׁה זוֹ לְלֵידַת יִצְחָק שֶׁאָז הָיוּ הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
and this exposition would be far more appropriate to the narrative of Isaac's birth, at which time all rejoiced, as the Midrash states.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּדָרַשׁ "צַדִּיק" עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא סְתָם צַדִּיק,
And it appears that it expounds “righteous person” (tzaddik) as referring to our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the archetype of the unqualified righteous one,
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁעוֹבֵר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה אַף דְּרַבָּנָן שׁוּב נִקְרָא רָשָׁע כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְבָמוֹת כ., נִדָּה יב.),
for once a person transgresses even a rabbinic precept he is subsequently termed wicked, as is written (Yevamot 20a, Niddah 12a),
וְאִם עוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה אַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה וְלֹא צַדִּיק.
and if he repents afterward he is designated a penitent (ba'al teshuvah) and not an absolute righteous person (tzaddik).
וְרַק יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל וְלֹא קִלְקֵל מֵעוֹלָם, שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע כְּלָל מֵהֲנָאַת הַגּוּף, הוּא נִקְרָא סְתָם צַדִּיק.
And only our father Jacob, peace be upon him—who was like Adam the First before the fall and never corrupted his ways, having never known any base physical pleasure—is called the consummate tzaddik.
וְדָרַשׁ עַל יִצְחָק "גִּיל יָגִיל אֲבִי צַדִּיק",
And the Midrash expounds concerning Isaac: “The father of a righteous person shall greatly rejoice,”
וְהַיְינוּ יִצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה אֲבִי יַעֲקֹב,
namely Isaac, who was the father of Jacob,
וְהוּא שִׂימַּח אֲחֵרִים גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁכְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק הָיוּ הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים,
and he brought joy to others as well, for when Isaac was born all rejoiced,
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
since once Isaac was born, who was the very first to be circumcised at eight days,
יָדְעוּ שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ רָאוּי שֶׁיֵּצֵא נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק,
they knew that from him the soul of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who was truly righteous, was destined to emerge,
אַחַר שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ הַפְּסוֹלֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁב כְּלָל לְזַרְעוֹ.
after the dross (Esau), who is not considered his seed at all, would be separated from him.
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ "וְיוֹלֵד חָכָם יִשְׂמַח בּוֹ" גַּם כֵּן עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא סְתָם חָכָם,
And likewise, “and he who fathers a wise child shall rejoice in him” is expounded regarding our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who is the archetype of the wise man,
דְּאַף דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלִּימֵּד תּוֹרָה וְקִיַּם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא כח:),
for although our father Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first who taught Torah and fulfilled the entire Torah, as is written (Yoma 28b),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם סְתָם חָכָם הוּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
nonetheless the ultimate wise one is our father Jacob, peace be upon him,
דִּכְתִיב: "תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב",
as it is written: “You will show truth to Jacob,”
אֱמֶת זוֹ תּוֹרָה (בְּרָכוֹת ה:).
and “truth” refers to the Torah (Berakhot 5b).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק",
And this is what Scripture states: “These are the generations of Isaac, the son of Abraham: Abraham fathered Isaac,”
שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוֹרִיד הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּבוֹ הִתְחִיל הַשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה,
in that our father Abraham brought down the words of Torah and with him began the two millennia of Torah,
וְהוּא הוֹפִיעַ בְּיִצְחָק,
and this spiritual light shone forth within Isaac,
וּכְשֶׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה הָיוּ הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִים בּוֹ,
and when Isaac was born, being circumcised at eight days, all rejoiced in him,
שֶׁכְּבָר רָאוּי לְהוֹלִיד נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא סְתָם צַדִּיק וְחָכָם כָּאָמוּר.
for he was now fit to father the soul of Jacob, who is the archetype of the righteous and the wise, as stated.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא:
And afterward it is stated in Midrash Tanchuma:
זֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב: "עֲטֶרֶת זְקֵנִים בְּנֵי בָנִים וְגוֹמֵר",
This is what Scripture stated: “The crown of old men is grandchildren, etc.,”
אַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב כוּלֵי,
Abraham was crowned through the merit of Jacob, etc.;
אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, לָזֶה אַתָּה מַצִּיל, כַּמָּה רְשָׁעִים עֲתִידִין לַעֲמוֹד מִמֶּנּוּ?
the ministering angels said: Master of the Universe, to this one are You delivering? How many wicked ones are destined to arise from him!
אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: בִּשְׁבִיל יַעֲקֹב בֶּן בְּנוֹ כוּלֵי.
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: On account of Jacob, his grandson, etc.
וְאֵינוֹ מוּבָן,
And this is difficult to understand,
דִּלְשׁוֹן מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לֹא מָצִינוּ עַל שָׂטָן וּמְקַטְרֵג,
for the title “ministering angels” is never found to designate Satan or an accusing adversary,
וְלָמָּה קִטְרְגוּ כָּאן?
so why did they bring accusations here?
גַּם אֵיךְ יֹאמְרוּ שֶׁשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין שֶׁלֹּא לְהַצִּילוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִפְּנֵי הָרְשָׁעִים שֶׁעֲתִידִין לַעֲמוֹד מִמֶּנּוּ,
Furthermore, how could they argue that strict justice dictates not to rescue him, Heaven forbid, because of the wicked destined to descend from him?
הֲלֹא אֲפִילּוּ בְּמִי שֶׁעָתִיד לְקַלְקֵל בְּעַצְמוֹ מָצִינוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה טז:) שֶׁאֵין דָּנִין אֶת הָאָדָם אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה!
For even concerning one who is himself destined to degenerate, we find (Rosh Hashanah 16b) that a person is judged only according to his deeds at that immediate hour!
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בְּ"יְפֵה תֹּאַר" שֶׁמִּי שֶׁמּוֹסֵר נַפְשׁוֹ עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם אֵין מַצִּילִין אוֹתוֹ רַק לְצוֹרֶךְ אֲחֵרִים,
And what is written in Yefeh To'ar—that one who sacrifices his life for the Sanctification of the Name is not miraculously delivered except for the necessity of others,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ טוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הִצִּילוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
as it is to his own spiritual benefit to give up his life, just as they did not deliver Rabbi Akiva, see there—
גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ מוּבָן,
this too is difficult to understand,
שֶׁהֲרֵי גַּם בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מָצִינוּ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ: "זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ?",
for even regarding Rabbi Akiva we find that Moses our teacher questioned: “Is this Torah and this its reward?”
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר לוֹ: "שְׁתוֹק, כָּךְ עָלָה בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה לְפָנַי" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת כט:),
and that which He answered him: “Be silent, so it arose in thought before Me,” as is written (Menachot 29b),
פֵּירְשׁוּ שֶׁהַמְּכֻוָּון עַל מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
commentators explained that this refers to the conscious yearning of Rabbi Akiva itself.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרְצוֹן רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא זֶה הָיָה, שֶׁהִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לָזֶה,
Namely, that this was the very will of Rabbi Akiva, who deeply craved this martyrdom,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת סא:): "כָּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מִצְטַעֵר עַל פָּסוּק זֶה וְכוּלֵי, מָתַי יָבֹא לְיָדִי וַאֲקַיְּמֶנּוּ",
as is written (Berakhot 61b): “All my days I was grieved over this verse, etc., saying: when will it come to my hand that I may fulfill it?”
וְזֶה לֹא מָצִינוּ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
and such an explicit yearning we do not find by our father Abraham, peace be upon him.
גַּם לְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ דְּקָאֵי עַל מַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
Furthermore, according to its simple reading that it refers to the thought of Hashem, blessed be He,
הַמְּכֻוָּון עַל מַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית" שֶׁבּוֹ הוּזְכַּר תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחֹשֶׁךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ "יְהִי אוֹר",
the intention points to the primordial utterance of Creation wherein unformed void and darkness are mentioned, and subsequently “Let there be light,”
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קפד א),
for there is no light except that which issues from within darkness (Zohar II, 184a),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הוּצְרַךְ לָזֶה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כֵּן זָכָה לְמַדְרֵגָתוֹ,
meaning that Rabbi Akiva required this ordeal, through which he merited his exalted level,
מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב: "כָּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ" – זֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵירָיו,
as written: “His eye saw every precious thing”—this refers to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues,
דְּבָרִים שֶׁלֹּא נִגְלוּ לְמֹשֶׁה נִגְלוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וַחֲבֵירָיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת),
matters that were not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues, as written (Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma, Chukat),
וְהוּא שַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁנִּמְסַר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה וְלֹא נִגְלָה לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:),
and this is the Fiftieth Gate which is transmitted to a master of repentance and was not revealed to Moses our teacher, as written in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 21b),
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ נוֹלַד טוֹב וְנִתְמַלֵּא הַבַּיִת אוֹר וְלֹא קִלְקֵל מֵעוֹלָם;
because Moses our teacher was born good, the house being filled with light, and he never sinned;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (פְּסָחִים מט:) שֶׁאָמַר: "כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי עַם הָאָרֶץ אָמַרְתִּי: מִי יִתֵּן כוּלֵי",
whereas regarding Rabbi Akiva we find (Pesachim 49b) that he said: “When I was an unlearned person I used to say: Who will give me, etc.,”
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי זָכָה לְשַׁעַר הַחֲמִשִּׁים הַנִּמְסָר לְבַעַל תְּשׁוּבָה.
and on this account he merited the Fiftieth Gate given to a penitent.
וְזָכָה לָזֶה עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִשְׁתּוֹקֵק כָּל יָמָיו עַל קִדּוּשׁ הַשֵּׁם: "מָתַי יָבֹא לְיָדִי וַאֲקַיְּמֶנּוּ", וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מְיוּחָד בָּזֶה.
And he merited this because he yearned all his days for the Sanctification of the Name, saying: “When will it come to my hand that I may fulfill it,” and he was unique in this.
אֲבָל בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהָיָה רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁקִּיַּם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ וְלִימֵּד תּוֹרָה וּמָסַר נַפְשׁוֹ עַל קְדוּשַּׁת שְׁמוֹ,
However, with our father Abraham, peace be upon him, who was the first to fulfill the entire Torah, who taught Torah, and who sacrificed his life for the sanctification of His Name,
הָיוּ צְרִיכִין הַמַּלְאָכִים לוֹמַר "זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְזוֹ שְׂכָרָהּ?" וּלְלַמֵּד זְכוּת עָלָיו,
the angels should have exclaimed, “Is this Torah and this its reward?” and defended his merit!

and so here, as long as they did not know that our father Jacob, peace be upon him, would descend from him—destined to bring forth twelve tribes in whom there was no blemish—

they assumed that from him too wicked descendants would arise and that the mixture of good and evil would persist until Adam the First rectifies the flaw.

And afterward the Midrash states: And from where do we derive that children are crowned on account of fathers, etc.?
מָה יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר לְלָבָן: "לוּלֵי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וּפַחַד יִצְחָק וְגוֹמֵר",
What did Jacob say to Laban: “Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac had been with me, etc.”
הֱוֵי זְכוּת אַבְרָהָם הִצִּילַתְהוּ לְיַעֲקֹב כוּלֵי.
Thus, the merit of Abraham rescued Jacob, etc.
וְהִנֵּה בַּפָּסוּק נִזְכַּר גַּם יִצְחָק, וְהַמִּדְרָשׁ מַסִּיק רַק זְכוּת אַבְרָהָם.
Now behold, in the verse Isaac is also mentioned, yet the Midrash concludes solely with the merit of Abraham.
גַּם הַפָּסוּק שֶׁדָּרַשׁ "וְתִפְאֶרֶת בָּנִים אֲבוֹתָם" גַּם כֵּן נִזְכַּר לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים.
Furthermore, the verse expounded, “and the glory of children is their fathers,” is likewise stated in the plural.
אַךְ עִנְיַן הַדְּרָשׁ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת נח.): "וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת" – זוֹ מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
However, the inner meaning of this exposition is based on what is written in the Gemara (Berakhot 58a): “And the glory”—this refers to the Giving of the Torah;
וְעִיקַּר הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁזִּיכָּה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְזַרְעוֹ
and the primary “great substance” that our father Abraham, peace be upon him, bequeathed to his descendants
שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ עַל יְדֵי יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
was that through the Exodus from Egypt they would merit the Giving of the Torah,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ אֶת הָעָם מִמִּצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר",
as it is stated: “When you have brought forth the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain,”
וְזֶה יוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת רַק כְּשֶׁיִּזְכּוּ שֶׁיֻּכְלַל בָּהֶם קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק,
and this they could merit only when they merited to integrate within themselves the holiness of Abraham and Isaac.
שֶׁשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה: "אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה",
For the roots of the words of Torah are “I am” and “You shall not have,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת "יִשָּׁקֵנִי")
and as written (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, Parashat Yishakeini)
שֶׁבְּדִבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" נִתְקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם וּבְדִבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה" נֶעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבָּם.
that through the utterance “I am” Torah study was implanted in their hearts, and through the utterance “You shall not have” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts.
"אָנֹכִי" כּוֹלֵל כָּל רְמַ״ח מִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה, וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה" כּוֹלֵל כָּל שְׁסַ״ה מִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
“I am” encompasses all 248 positive commandments, and “You shall not have” encompasses all 365 negative commandments.
וּקְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה,
And the holiness of our father Abraham was active devotion to positive commandments,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (חֻלִּין טז.): קְרָא זְרִיזוּתֵיהּ דְּאַבְרָהָם קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן,
as is written (Chullin 16a): the verse comes to teach us the alacrity of Abraham,
וּזְרִיזוּת הוּא בְּמִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רַשִׁ״י לָרִי״ף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה),
and alacrity applies to positive commandments, as Rashi writes on the Rif (Avodah Zarah ch. 1),
וְהוּא בָּא עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבָה מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
and this flows from love, the essential attribute of our father Abraham.
וּקְדוּשַׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַיִּרְאָה – "פַּחַד יִצְחָק",
And the holiness of our father Isaac, peace be upon him, was fear/awe—“the Fear of Isaac”—
שֶׁמִּזֶּה בָּא לִזְהִירוּת בְּמִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
from which stems vigilant care in negative commandments,
וְהַיְינוּ לַעֲקוֹר הָרָע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ.
which means uprooting evil from the foolish heart at one's left.
וְעִיקַּר הָרְכוּשׁ גָּדוֹל דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And the essence of that great substance of the Giving of the Torah
שֶׁיִּתָּקַע תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" – וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי זְכוּת אַבְרָהָם.
was that Torah study be fixed in their hearts through the utterance “I am”—and this is through the merit of Abraham.
אַךְ לֹא יוּכְלוּ לִזְכּוֹת לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה עַד שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ בְּמִדַּת סוּר מֵרָע לְהוֹרִיק הָרָע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל, וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי מִדַּת פַּחַד יִצְחָק.

Yet they could not merit the words of Torah until they were refined in the trait of turning from evil to purge the malice from the foolish heart, and this is through the attribute of the Fear of Isaac.

And this is what is stated: “And the glory of children is their fathers,”

referring to the community of Israel who merited the Giving of the Torah which is titled “glory,”

which is through their fathers, the holiness of Abraham and Isaac.

Nonetheless, the primary foundation is through the merit of Abraham;

only that in addition to this was required “and the Fear of Isaac,”

for without the attribute of awe they could not merit the holiness of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, to implant the study of Torah via the utterance “I am” in the heart, as stated.

And through this he was preserved, ensuring his descendants would merit the Giving of the Torah, which is the ultimate merit of Abraham.

p: וּמַסִּיק בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא: יִצְחָק נִתְעַטֵּר בְּאַבְרָהָם וְאַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בְּיִצְחָק.
And the Midrash Tanchuma concludes: Isaac was crowned through Abraham, and Abraham was crowned through Isaac.
וְהַיְינוּ לְפָרֵשׁ כֶּפֶל הַלָּשׁוֹן: "יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק".
Namely, this explains the textual redundancy: “Isaac, son of Abraham: Abraham fathered Isaac.”
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְהָבִין לְשׁוֹן "נִתְעַטֵּר", גַּם לָמָּה נִכְתַּב זֶה בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ וְלֹא בְּלֵידַת יִצְחָק.
Yet one must understand the term “was crowned” (nit'ater), and also why this is recorded specifically in this portion rather than at the birth of Isaac.
אֲבָל הָעִנְיָן דִּלְשׁוֹן עֲטָרָה הוּא כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלָם בְּכָל עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת עַד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
However, the matter is that the term “crown” applies when one reaches completion across all ten sefirot up to Keter Elyon (the Supreme Crown),
כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים", בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
in the manner of the verse: “And Abraham was old, advanced in days”—meaning in those supernal days, as written in the holy Zohar,
וְזָכָה לְמִדַּת זָקֵן שֶׁהוּא עַתִּיקָא,
and he merited the attribute of “Elder,” which corresponds to Atika Kadisha,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פז.): "עַד אַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה זִקְנָה",
and as we explained regarding that which is written in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 87a): “Until Abraham there was no old age,”
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מִי שֶׁזָּכָה לְמִדַּת זִקְנָה שֶׁהוּא כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא.
meaning that there had been no one who had attained the spiritual trait of supernal Eldership, which is achieved when one merits the disclosure of Atika.

meaning that he attained perfection in his spiritual attribute all the way to its root across all ten sefirot.

and this is the characteristic attribute of our father Isaac, peace be upon him,

since the attribute of our father Abraham was love, as it is said: “Abraham who loved Me.”

Now superficially, the Binding was performed out of love for Hashem, in that he suppressed his compassion for his only son,

casting aside the love for his son in the face of his love for Hashem.

Yet we have already explained that according to the standard trait of love of our father Abraham, he would have had reason to transgress the command of Hashem and not bind Isaac

in order that the Divinity of Hashem, blessed be His Name, might become known to the world through Isaac,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּסַר נַפְשׁוֹ בְּכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ אַף שֶׁהָיָה נֶגֶד הַדִּין וְלֹא הָיָה רַשַּׁאי כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר (נֹחַ מַאֲמָר ט),
just as he sacrificed his life in the fiery furnace even though it was technically contrary to the halakhic requirement and he was not legally permitted to do so, as explained (Noach, essay 9),

rather out of sheer love he sought to sanctify the Name even if he were to forfeit, Heaven forbid, his portion in the World to Come;
וְכֵן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּנִסָּיוֹן הָעֲקֵידָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ
and likewise he might have acted in the trial of the Binding—not listening to the command—
כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּשְׁאַר יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְיִתְפַּרְסֵם אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ עַל יָדוֹ.
in order that our father Isaac, peace be upon him, survive, so that His Divinity be promulgated through him.
אַךְ מִיִּרְאָתוֹ הַמֻּפְלֶגֶת יָרֵא לַעֲבוֹר פִּי ה',
Yet out of his extraordinary awe and reverence he feared to transgress the word of Hashem,
שֶׁחָשַׁד אֶת עַצְמוֹ פֶּן הוּא נוֹגֵעַ מַה בַּדָּבָר לְאַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ.
for he suspected himself lest he harbor a personal, selfish bias in the matter stemming from paternal love for his son.

and Abraham replied to him: “Such is the punishment of a liar, that even when he speaks truth he is not believed, etc.”;

and likewise from that which is written (Bereishit Rabbah 56): Satan said to him: Tomorrow He will say to you, 'You are a shedder of blood, etc.,' and Abraham answered him: Even on that condition, see there.

yet out of his intense awe he was terrified to violate the explicit command of Hashem,

and this is what Scripture states: “Now I know that you are a God-fearing man, etc.”

And this explains the statement: “Abraham was crowned through Isaac,”

meaning that the consummate perfection of our father Abraham up to Keter Elyon was actualized through the attribute of Isaac (Yir'ah).

And “Isaac was crowned through Abraham” is understood according to what the Rama of Fano wrote: the soul of the father is the mazal (supernal source) of the son.

as is written (Megillah 3a): “Even though they did not see, their mazal saw”;

“seeing” pertains to Chokhmah (Wisdom), while “mazala” pertains to Atika,

as written in the holy Zohar (III, 79b): life, children, and sustenance depend upon mazala which is Atika, see there;

and this is what they meant that “Isaac was crowned through Abraham”—that when he attained perfection up to Keter Elyon, it was achieved by becoming complete in the attribute of Abraham (Ahavah).

And this is what is stated: “These are the generations of Isaac, etc.”
וְהַיְינוּ נֶפֶשׁ יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהָיָה מִצִּדּוֹ נִשְׁלָם כְּבָר מִכֹּל וָכֹל מִתּוֹלָדָה,
namely the soul of Jacob, who on his part was already perfected in every respect from birth,
שֶׁהָיָה כּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק,
in that he incorporated within himself the holiness of both Abraham and Isaac,
וְהָיָה עֵסֶק שֶׁלּוֹ רַק שֶׁתִּהְיֶה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה.
and his singular life's work was merely that his bed be spiritually whole (free of flawed offspring).

And the birth of the soul of Jacob was impossible until Abraham and Isaac were perfected to the very root:
אַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בְּיִצְחָק וְיִצְחָק נִתְעַטֵּר בְּאַבְרָהָם,
Abraham was crowned through Isaac and Isaac was crowned through Abraham,

and only then could Isaac bring forth the soul of our father Jacob, peace be upon him, who would father the Jewish nation.
וְאַף שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ נִזְכַּר גַּם לֵידַת עֵשָׂו,
And even though in this weekly portion the birth of Esau is also mentioned,
אַךְ כְּבָר כָּתַבְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ: "אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ",
yet we have already written concerning the statement of our father Jacob, “I am Esau your firstborn,”
וְאֵיךְ הוֹצִיא מִפִּיו דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ?
asking: how could he utter from his mouth a statement that was not true?
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קמג א) אִיתָא שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל אָז: "הַצִּילָה נַפְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת שָׁקֶר".
And in the holy Zohar (I, 143a) it is brought that he prayed at that moment: “Deliver my soul from lying lips.”
אַךְ בַּמֶּה שֶׁלָּבַשׁ בִּגְדֵי עֵשָׂו הוֹצִיא כָּל הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת מֵעֵשָׂו,
However, by donning the garments of Esau he extracted all the holy sparks from Esau,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמַּה שֶּׁמָּצָא עֵשָׂו חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ הוּא הַנִּיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ, וְזֶה כְּבָר בְּיָדִי: "אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ".
and this is what he communicated: that which caused Esau to find favor in your eyes was the holy sparks within him, and these are now in my possession: “I am Esau your firstborn.”
וְאִיתָא מֵהָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו" –
And it is taught from the Ari, of blessed memory, on the verse “because game was in his mouth”—
דְּקָאֵי עַל נִשְׁמַת רַבִּי מֵאִיר דִּנְפַק מִנִּירוֹן כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (גִּיטִּין נו.),
that this refers to the soul of Rabbi Meir who descended from the Roman emperor Nero, as written (Gittin 56a),
וְהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה – סְתָם מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
and he is the root of the Oral Torah, as an anonymous Mishnah is Rabbi Meir.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו וְגוֹמֵר",
And this is the meaning of “I am Esau, etc.”:
שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁנָּשָׂא חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ מֵעֵשָׂו זֶהוּ בְּיָדִי וְאָנֹכִי הוּא.
that the holiness which found favor in your eyes from Esau is in my hand, and I am its bearer.
וְעִיקַּר הַפָּרָשָׁה לֵידַת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
And the primary theme of the portion is the birth of Jacob from whom the Jewish nation emerged;
וְעַל כֵּן הִקְדִּים כָּאן שְׁלֵימוּת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ, שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה "נִתְעַטֵּר".
and therefore it prefaced here the completion of Abraham and Isaac to their ultimate root, which is indicated by the term “was crowned.”
וְנִתְעַטֵּר אַבְרָהָם בְּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה וְיִצְחָק בְּמִדַּת אַהֲבָה,
Abraham was crowned with the attribute of awe, and Isaac with the attribute of love,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א, קלג ב) דְּאִתְכְּלִיל מַיָּא בְּאֶשָּׁא וְאֶשָּׁא בְּמַיָּא,
as is written (in the holy Zohar I, 133b) that water was merged into fire and fire into water,
דִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה כְּשֶׁבָּא עַל יָדָהּ לְיִרְאָה עִלָּאָה,
for the perfection of love is when through it one attains supreme awe,
וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה – הָאַהֲבָה,
and the perfection of awe is love,
